sections.title: Test Coverage Analysis — `src/job_dashboard`
sections.content: Reviewed 8 source modules (593 lines) against 32 existing tests across `tests/`. Testing conventions used throughout: `tmp_path` for sqlite, `monkeypatch` + `tests.conftest.FakeResponse` for HTTP sources. I followed the same style below.

sections.title: Summary of gaps by severity
sections.content:
| Area | Gap | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| `db.py` | `jobs_needing_embed_score` never tested against a **duplicate** job | High — dedup+matching interaction untested |
| `db.py` | `record_llm_evaluation` success path never asserts stored `strengths/gaps/flags` JSON | High — silent JSON corruption possible |
| `db.py` | `record_llm_evaluation` type-check branch (`not isinstance(llm_score, int)`) untested | Medium |
| `ingest.py` | `company_sources` exception isolation untested (only `job_sources` is) | High — asymmetric coverage of duplicated logic |
| All `requests`-based sources | HTTP error (`raise_for_status`) propagation untested in every module | High — silent failures possible in prod |
| `remoteok_source.py` | `location` fallback, `job_url` fallback, non-"contract" `job_type` branch, salary edge cases untested | Medium |
| `himalayas_source.py`/`remotive_source.py` | `_format_salary`/salary-fallback partial-data branches untested | Medium |
| `wwr_source.py` | Title without `:` separator (→ `"Unknown"` company) untested | Low |
| `profile_text.py` | Evaluation file present but regex doesn't match (no `**Career goals:**` section) untested | Low |
| Integration | No test exercises a real source fetcher through `run_ingest` → `db` end-to-end | Medium |

---

sections.title: 1. `db.py` — `jobs_needing_embed_score` ignores duplicates (untested)
sections.content:
```python
def test_duplicate_job_excluded_from_needing_embed_score(tmp_path):
    conn = init_db(tmp_path / "t.db")
    insert_job(conn, _job(1))
    insert_job(conn, _job(2))
    ids = [r[0] for r in conn.execute("SELECT id FROM jobs ORDER BY id").fetchall()]
    mark_duplicate(conn, ids[1], ids[0])

    needing = jobs_needing_embed_score(conn, "hashA")

    assert [row[0] for row in needing] == [ids[0]]
```

sections.title: 2. `db.py` — `record_llm_evaluation` success path doesn't verify stored fields
sections.content:
```python
def test_record_llm_evaluation_stores_json_fields(tmp_path):
    conn = init_db(tmp_path / "t.db")
    insert_job(conn, _job(1))
    job_id = conn.execute("SELECT id FROM jobs").fetchone()[0]
    upsert_embed_score(conn, job_id, 0.8, "h")

    record_llm_evaluation(
        conn, job_id, 74, "Good Fit",
        strengths=["Python"], gaps=["No Rust"], flags={"visa": True},
    )

    row = conn.execute(
        "SELECT llm_score, verdict, strengths, gaps, flags, llm_scored_at "
        "FROM match_scores WHERE job_id = ?", (job_id,),
    ).fetchone()
    assert row[0] == 74
    assert row[1] == "Good Fit"
    assert json.loads(row[2]) == ["Python"]
    assert json.loads(row[3]) == ["No Rust"]
    assert json.loads(row[4]) == {"visa": True}
    assert row[5] is not None
```

sections.title: 3. `db.py` — non-int `llm_score` type check
sections.content:
```python
def test_record_llm_evaluation_rejects_non_int_score(tmp_path):
    conn = init_db(tmp_path / "t.db")
    insert_job(conn, _job(1))
    job_id = conn.execute("SELECT id FROM jobs").fetchone()[0]
    upsert_embed_score(conn, job_id, 0.8, "h")

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        record_llm_evaluation(conn, job_id, 74.5, "Good Fit", [], [], {})
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        record_llm_evaluation(conn, job_id, "74", "Good Fit", [], [], {})
```

sections.title: 4. `ingest.py` — company source failure isolation (mirror of job-source test, currently missing)
sections.content:
```python
def test_run_ingest_isolates_a_failing_company_source(tmp_path):
    conn = init_db(tmp_path / "test.db")
    good_company = Company(name="Acme", funding_amount="$1M")

    def boom():
        raise RuntimeError("sheet unreachable")

    result = ingest.run_ingest(
        conn,
        job_sources=[],
        company_sources=[boom, lambda: [good_company]],
    )

    assert result == {"new_jobs": 0, "companies_seen": 1, "source_errors": 1}
    row_count = conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM companies").fetchone()[0]
    assert row_count == 1
```

sections.title: 5. HTTP error propagation — untested in every `requests`-based source (himalayas, remoteok, remotive, startup_sheet)
sections.content:
`FakeResponse.raise_for_status` already supports this via `status_code`; no test exercises it. Example for `remotive_source.py` (repeat pattern for the other three):

```python
def test_fetch_remotive_jobs_propagates_http_errors(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        remotive_source.requests, "get",
        lambda *a, **k: FakeResponse(status_code=503),
    )

    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        remotive_source.fetch_remotive_jobs("AI engineer")
```

sections.title: 6. `remoteok_source.py` — several untested branches
sections.content:
```python
def test_fetch_remoteok_jobs_defaults_location_and_falls_back_job_url(monkeypatch):
    payload = [
        {"legal": "..."},
        {
            "id": "1", "position": "Backend Eng", "company": "Co",
            "location": "", "description": "desc",
            "apply_url": None, "url": "https://remoteok.com/remote-jobs/1",
            "tags": ["python"],  # no "contract" tag
        },
    ]
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        remoteok_source.requests, "get", lambda *a, **k: FakeResponse(json_data=payload)
    )

    jobs = remoteok_source.fetch_remoteok_jobs()

    assert jobs[0].location == "Remote"
    assert jobs[0].job_url == "https://remoteok.com/remote-jobs/1"
    assert jobs[0].job_type is None  # no "contract" tag present


def test_fetch_remoteok_jobs_salary_missing_both_bounds(monkeypatch):
    payload = [
        {"legal": "..."},
        {"id": "1", "position": "Eng", "company": "Co", "location": "",
         "description": "desc", "apply_url": "https://x/1"},
    ]
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        remoteok_source.requests, "get", lambda *a, **k: FakeResponse(json_data=payload)
    )

    jobs = remoteok_source.fetch_remoteok_jobs()
    assert jobs[0].salary_text is None
```

    rss = SAMPLE_RSS.replace(

    real_parse = feedparser.parse

sections.title: 9. `profile_text.py` — evaluation file present but no matching section
sections.content:
```python
def test_evaluation_file_without_career_goals_section_is_ignored(tmp_path):
    profile = tmp_path / "01.md"
    evaluation = tmp_path / "04.md"
    profile.write_text(PROFILE_MD)
    evaluation.write_text("# Job Evaluation Framework\nNo goals section here.\n")

    result = compose_profile_text(profile, evaluation)

    assert "Target Roles & Career Goals" not in result.text
```

sections.title: 10. Integration gap — no test wires a real source module through `run_ingest` into `db`
sections.content:
Every existing `ingest.py` test uses hand-built `JobListing`/`Company` objects, never a real source fetcher. Recommend one smoke test per pipeline stage boundary, e.g.:

```python
def test_run_ingest_end_to_end_with_real_source_module(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    conn = init_db(tmp_path / "t.db")
    payload = {"jobs": [{
        "guid": "abc", "title": "ML Engineer", "companyName": "Acme",
        "locationRestrictions": ["US"], "description": "desc",
        "applicationLink": "https://himalayas.app/jobs/abc",
    }]}
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        himalayas_source.requests, "get", lambda *a, **k: FakeResponse(json_data=payload)
    )

    result = ingest.run_ingest(
        conn,
        job_sources=[lambda: himalayas_source.fetch_himalayas_jobs("ml")],
        company_sources=[],
    )

    assert result["new_jobs"] == 1
    assert job_exists(conn, "https://himalayas.app/jobs/abc")
```

---

**Not covered by this pass (out of scope for `src/job_dashboard`):** `vendor/ai-job-search/` (has its own test suite already) and `.claude/` tooling scripts — treated as vendored/tooling code, not the primary project.

I wasn't able to run `pytest --cov` directly (command requires approval in this session) — the analysis above is from manual line-by-line comparison of each source module against its test file. If you want exact line/branch percentages, say the word and I'll get approval to run `pytest --cov=job_dashboard --cov-report=term-missing`.
